customTitle: Creating a p5.js sketch to shrink an image into a grid square

message.text: Let's make a new p5js sketch (in instance mode). The canvas will be a 600x600 square, and it will load a square image. The sketch will display the image at canvas size, then shrink it down to fit into a grid square (the square canvas can be dividied into a 10x10 grid of 60x60 squares). The shrinking will take 10 steps, and as the image shrinks from 600x600 at the canvas center, it will be drawn centered going towards the target grid square. Does this description make sense?

Excellent! I've saved this a de.zoom.grid.js, which you can use for further reference.

Now, let's modify the sketch to fill all the grid squares in sequence.

That's great! However, the completed images disappear as the p.draw function clears the canvas with each draw.

Maybe use a PGraphics or PImage object to hold the image of completed grids squares, paint that to the canvas, and paint the shrinking image on top of them?

Thanks! I've made a couple of changes to make thinks more configurable, introducing variables for the most part.

Now, I'd like to extract the shrinking code to a separate function.
Great! Now, can we make the tile order random, instead of sequential?
Nice, you're very helpful! I've modified the code slightly to stop completely when the grid is complete. It requires a repetition of p.image(pg, 0, 0). Is there a better method with less repetition?
Thank you. How can we change the shrinking algorithm from a smooth lerp to something that starts out slowly and increases the fewer steps remain?
The transition from shrunken image to canvas-size image (the next tile) is a bit jarring. Can we make the image slightly transparent for the first few steps? Lerping it in, so to speak?

Thanks! I'd like to change this shrinkSteps so that they speed up the fewer the steps remain. This should not be a constant change - it should be super slow at first - probably no change at all the first few cells. The shrinkSteps should never be faster than 5, however.
